payload.headline: Apple's cash keeps growing, but 356.27 still sits above every value estimate

summary.thesis: Apple is a strong, cash-rich business, but at 356.27 the price assumes faster cash-flow growth than its recent record supports, while analysts keep cutting estimates.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait for a lower price. Swing: wait, because there is no resistance level to set a target.
summary.act_at: Start buying at 321.32 or lower; add near 300.79

payload.happening: Apple closed at 356.27, up 0.39% on the day. It is moving sideways above its 50-day average of 338.92. Today's main news is a confirmed release-date announcement for the first Apple Home Collection smart devices, plus a report that Donald Trump wants Tim Cook to run Nvidia. The next earnings report is due 2027-01-28.
payload.business: Several things change the business itself, and most of them are good. Revenue over the last twelve months grew 15.06% to 478.8B. Free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) rose to 136.1B from 98.8B. Operating margin (profit per dollar of sales before interest and tax) went up to 33.01% from 31.97%. Two things are less good. Quarterly growth slowed to 11.72% from 16.6% two quarters earlier. And inventory is up 154% while quarterly sales are up 12%. If that stock doesn't sell, Apple may have to cut prices, which would hurt margins. That is the real risk to watch in the January report. The new Home devices add to demand but are not yet in any number we have. Other items mostly change sentiment or governance, not the business. The report about Tim Cook and Nvidia is only a report. If it led to a CEO change, that would be a leadership question (general knowledge), and nothing in the filings points to one. The latest annual report also adds a new risk on an investigation, which is a legal and governance item with no number attached. Cash generation and margins are not at risk today. What is at risk is how fast growth continues, and whether margins hold if inventory has to be cleared.

worth.text: At 356.27, buyers pay 39.7 times trailing earnings and 33.7 times next year's expected earnings. Price-to-sales is 10.8, against a peer median of 5.5, and sits at the 98th percentile of Apple's own last five years. A discounted cash flow model (DCF: today's value of future cash flows) puts fair value at 146.14 in the bear case, 226.4 in the base case and 321.32 in the bull case. Apple's own price-to-sales history gives 222.27 to 300.79. Every method lands below today's price. The gap comes down to one input: how fast free cash flow grows at the start. The current price implies starting growth of about 27.2%. At 20% growth, the model gives 270.61. You need about 30% growth to reach 395.94. For comparison, sales grew 15% last year and 8% a year over the last three years. Margins matter too. If operating margin fell to 24%, value would drop to 202.56. I put fair value at 226.4 to 321.32.
worth.key_assumption: Starting free cash flow growth: the price implies 27.2%, but recent sales growth was 15% last year and 8% a year over three years.

bull: Free cash flow jumped to 136.1B from 98.8B in a year, which pays for buybacks and new products.
Operating margin widened to 33.01% from 31.97%, so each dollar of sales is bringing in more profit.
Share count fell 1.56% over the year, so each remaining share owns a bigger slice of the profits.
bear: Price-to-sales of 10.8 is about double the peer median of 5.5 and at the 98th percentile of Apple's own five-year range.
Inventory is up 154% while quarterly sales are up only 12%, which could force price cuts and lower margins.
Analysts cut next-year EPS to 10.57 from 10.84 over 30 days (-2.5%), and the next-quarter estimate fell 3.8%.

levels.what: Today's close, above the top of every valuation range, which leaves little room for disappointment.
The DCF bull-case value and the top of my fair-value range. At or below this, buying starts to make sense.
The top of Apple's own price-to-sales history, close to the rising 200-day average of 300.97. A better price for adding.

longterm.why: This is a grade-B business with strong cash flow. But today's price needs cash-flow growth of about 27.2%, and estimates are falling.

swing.why: The trend is sideways and the 20-day average is flat. The data shows no resistance level to aim for, so there is no target and no way to judge reward against risk. Support zones sit at 351.16–355.11 and 342.99–347.89.

decision.timing: The 2027-01-28 report is the next real test of inventory and growth. January options (expiring 2027-01-15, before earnings) price a 7.6% move, and falling estimates are a reason not to act before the report.

change_mind: The price falls to 321.32 or lower while the next-year EPS estimate stays near 10.57. Buying would then start inside the fair-value range.
Estimate revisions turn positive again (the 30-day revision is now -2.47%), and the 2027-01-28 report shows inventory growth well below today's 154%.
A close below the 342.99–347.89 support zone. I would then wait for prices near 300.79 instead of 321.32.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait. The 2.5% cut to next-year EPS estimates (to 10.57) confirmed it, though the top of the fair-value range moved up to 321.32 from 313.15.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
